passages.text:
**Maya Okafor designs software that patients and clinicians use under stress.** At Lumen Health she
leads design for the patient app used by about 400,000 people, and she runs the company's
accessibility review. Before that she built the design system at Brightpath Bank. She came to design from nursing: she worked four years as a registered nurse before retraining,
which is why her research sessions start on hospital floors rather than in a lab.

Turning research into decisions a team can ship. At Lumen she replaced a quarterly research report
with a weekly two-page brief, and the share of roadmap items backed by user evidence rose from 30
percent to 75 percent. Accessibility as a design constraint, not an audit. She brought the patient app to WCAG 2.2 AA.

She does not write production code. She prototypes in Figma and Framer and reads React well
enough to review a pull request, but she has never shipped frontend code to production. She has not done brand or marketing design. Her work is product interfaces.

Role: Senior Product Designer. June 2023 to present. Chicago, IL. Stack: Figma, Framer, Maze, Dovetail, Jira
Measured: 400,000 monthly active patients on the app she leads; -38% missed appointments after the reminder redesign; WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility level of the patient app
**She redesigned appointment reminders, and missed appointments fell 38 percent** across the
clinics using the app. The redesign came from twelve shadowing sessions with front-desk staff. She leads a team of three designers and runs the weekly accessibility review for every product
team.

Role: Product Designer. August 2020 to May 2023. Remote. Stack: Figma, Storybook, Zeroheight
Measured: 140 components in the design system she built; -45% time to ship a new screen after the system launched
She built Brightpath's first design system, 140 components in Figma with matching React tokens,
and the time to ship a new screen fell 45 percent. She designed the mobile check-deposit flow, which cut support calls about deposits by 22 percent.

Role: Registered Nurse. July 2015 to June 2019. Chicago, IL. She worked on a cardiac step-down unit. She led the unit's switch from paper to electronic bedside
charting, training 30 nurses.

A volunteer project: a map of free clinics in Chicago, built with two engineers. About 9,000
people used it in its first year. She ran the research and the design.

Master of Design, Human-Centered Design, Illinois Institute of Technology, 2020. Chicago, IL. Bachelor of Science in Nursing, Loyola University Chicago, 2015. She teaches an evening course in accessible design at a Chicago community college.

Design: interaction design, design systems, prototyping, usability testing, journey mapping. Tools: Figma, Framer, Maze, Dovetail, Storybook. Accessibility: WCAG 2.2, screen reader testing with VoiceOver and NVDA. Languages: English, Yoruba.
Core77 Design Award, 2022, for the check-deposit flow.

Available from March 2027. Looking for senior or lead product design roles in healthcare or
public-interest software. Hybrid in Chicago or remote.
